about: Every demo on the site: title, one line description and tags, grouped by subject. Source for the course pages (tools/courses.py), the teaching notes index (tools/notes.py) and the QR check (tools/qr.py). The order within a subject is the display order.

demos.title: Reasons for Seasons
demos.desc: Earth's tilted axis, the Sun's path across your sky, day length and sunlight through the year, and why distance from the Sun is not the reason.

demos.title: Moon Phases
demos.desc: Drag the Moon around Earth and see its phase from the ground, when it rises and sets, and why eclipses only happen in eclipse seasons.

demos.title: Gravity Near Earth
demos.desc: How g changes with height and latitude: from sea level to the space station and geostationary orbit, and how Earth's spin takes a little off at the equator.

demos.title: Kepler's Laws
demos.desc: Launch a planet by dragging its velocity arrow. Watch ellipses form, equal areas sweep out in equal times, and the orbit land on P² = a³/M with the real planets.

demos.title: GPS Clocks and Relativity
demos.desc: Why a GPS satellite's clock gains 38 microseconds a day: gravity makes higher clocks run fast, speed makes moving clocks run slow.

demos.title: Stellar Evolution
demos.desc: Follow a star of any mass across the HR diagram from the main sequence to a cooling white dwarf or a supernova, and date a star cluster from its turnoff.

demos.title: Finding Exoplanets
demos.desc: Watch a planet tug its star and cross its face, with the transit light curve and radial velocity curve drawing live. See why Earth twins are so hard to find.

demos.title: Cosmic Distance Ladder
demos.desc: Measure a parallax from two photos, time a Cepheid's light curve, find a supernova's peak, and fit Hubble's law to galaxy redshifts. Each rung calibrates the next.

demos.title: Tides
demos.desc: See why the Moon raises two ocean bulges, not one: subtract the pull at Earth's center from the pull everywhere else. Watch a city's tides over a day and spring and neap tides over a month.

demos.title: Star Slice
demos.desc: Cut a real MESA star model in half and zoom from the envelope to the core: composition, convection zones, burning shells, and a white dwarf crystallizing from the center out.

demos.title: Galaxy Rotation Curves
demos.desc: Stars far from a galaxy's center orbit as fast as those near it, though the visible matter says they should slow down. Build the curve from a bulge, disk, gas and a dark matter halo, measure it with Doppler shifts, and compare the Milky Way and NGC 3198.

demos.title: Black Holes and Lensing
demos.desc: Slide a galaxy behind a lens to make an Einstein ring, watch a microlensing event brighten, ray trace a black hole's shadow exactly, and see what gravity does to clocks, light and a person near Sagittarius A* and a stellar black hole.

demos.title: Lagrange Points
demos.desc: Drop or throw test particles in the rotating frame of two orbiting bodies: the five Lagrange points, zero velocity curves, Jupiter's Trojans, tadpole and horseshoe orbits, and halo style orbits near JWST's L2.

demos.title: White Dwarf Cooling
demos.desc: Watch a white dwarf fade: Mestel's cooling law, the core freezing from the center out once the ion coupling reaches 175, the latent heat that slows it, the Gaia Q branch and white dwarfs as a cosmic clock.

demos.title: Photoelectric Effect
demos.desc: Shine light on a metal, find the stopping voltage, and measure Planck's constant from the slope, the way Millikan did in 1916.

demos.title: Spectra Explorer
demos.desc: Click any of 99 elements to see its emission or absorption lines, measured by NIST. Includes the Bohr model of hydrogen and a mystery spectrum game, including a star.

demos.title: Spacetime Diagrams
demos.desc: Place events on a Minkowski diagram and change observers. Light cones stay at 45° while simultaneity, clocks and lengths change, through the train, the rod and the twin paradox.

demos.title: Quantum Wave Packets
demos.desc: Launch an electron at a barrier and watch part of it tunnel through, settle into energy eigenstates in a box or an oscillator, and collapse when you measure where it is.

demos.title: Hydrogen Orbitals
demos.desc: Every hydrogen state up to n = 6 as a 3D cloud sampled from |ψ|², a slice showing its nodes, and its radial probability against the Bohr orbit. Mix 1s and 2p and watch the charge slosh at the Lyman α frequency.

demos.title: Double Slit, One Particle at a Time
demos.desc: Fire photons, electrons or buckyballs through two slits one at a time. Single dots pile up into fringes, and a which slit detector washes them out.

demos.title: Radioactive Decay
demos.desc: A grid of nuclei that each decay at random, and a count that halves every half life anyway. Carbon 14 dating, iodine 131 and decay chains where a daughter builds up and dies away.

demos.title: Rutherford Scattering
demos.desc: Fire alpha particles at a gold nucleus one at a time or as a beam, count them by angle against 1/sin⁴(θ/2), and see why Thomson's plum pudding atom can never send one back.

demos.title: Nuclear Binding Energy
demos.desc: The curve of binding energy from 2,550 measured AME2020 masses: why fusing light nuclei and splitting heavy ones both release energy, why stars stop at iron, the liquid drop model term by term, magic numbers and the chart of nuclides.

demos.title: Compton Scattering
demos.desc: A photon bounces off a free electron and comes away with a longer wavelength. Drag the scattered photon around to see the shift, the electron's recoil and the momentum triangle, from Compton's 1923 x rays to cesium 137 gamma rays and the Compton edge.

demos.title: Lasers and Stimulated Emission
demos.desc: A photon can make an excited atom emit an exact copy of itself. See why there is no laser without population inversion, find the threshold of an Nd:YAG laser, watch it spike as it switches on, compare ruby, Nd:YAG and He–Ne levels, and count cavity modes.

demos.title: Franck–Hertz Experiment
demos.desc: Sweep the accelerating voltage across a mercury tube and watch the collector current drop every 4.9 V, then mark the peaks and fit their spacing like in the lab. Switch to neon to see glowing layers march toward the cathode.

demos.title: Gamma Spectroscopy
demos.desc: A virtual NaI(Tl) spectrometer in a lead castle: set the high voltage and gain, acquire Cs-137, Co-60, Na-22 or Ba-133 spectra on a multichannel analyzer, mark peaks, calibrate, measure resolution and lead attenuation, and identify an unknown source.

demos.title: Spin Resonance
demos.desc: Tune an electron or proton spin resonance probe, sweep the field, find the absorption peak on the oscilloscope, and measure g for DPPH and the gyromagnetic ratios of hydrogen and fluorine.

demos.title: Speed of Light
demos.desc: Foucault's rotating mirror bench: spin the mirror, read the shifted image on the microscope micrometer, and fit your readings for c.

demos.title: e/m of the Electron
demos.desc: Bend an electron beam into a glowing circle with Helmholtz coils, read its radius on the mirrored scale without parallax, and measure the charge to mass ratio.

demos.title: Electron Diffraction
demos.desc: Fire electrons through graphite, measure the two rings on the tube's screen at several voltages, and find the lattice spacings from de Broglie's λ = h/p.

demos.title: DNA in 3D
demos.desc: Build a DNA double helix atom by atom from any sequence or a random one: B and A forms, ball and stick, space filling or cartoon, hydrogen bonds, the two grooves, and a PDB export.

demos.title: Units, Scales and Estimates
demos.desc: The first week toolkit: zoom through 42 powers of ten from the observable universe to a proton, exact unit conversions, dimensional analysis, significant figures and Fermi estimates.

demos.title: Vectors and Relative Motion
demos.desc: Drag arrow tips to see components, sums, differences, and dot and cross products, steer a boat across a river where its velocity adds to the current's, and balance hanging masses on a force table.

demos.title: Motion Graphs
demos.desc: Position, velocity and acceleration graphs of a cart, linked: each is the slope of the one above and the area under it is the change in the one above. Then try to walk a target graph yourself.

demos.title: Forces and Friction
demos.desc: A block on a ramp you can tilt, push at an angle and tie to a hanging mass, with its free body diagram drawn to scale. Find where it slips, then time it to measure kinetic friction.

demos.title: Elevator: Apparent Weight
demos.desc: Ride an elevator standing on a scale. It reads more or less than your weight only while the elevator speeds up or slows down, and zero if the cable snaps.

demos.title: Circular Motion
demos.desc: What supplies mv²/r? Whirl a ball on a string and cut it, take a car round a flat or banked curve until it slides, speed up or brake on the curve, and send a ball round a vertical loop, with the free body diagram for each.

demos.title: Projectile Range
demos.desc: Fire baseballs, ping pong balls, cannonballs and more with and without air resistance, stack up to eight shots of different mass, size, drag or air density, and compare their paths and x, y and speed graphs side by side.

demos.title: Ball Launched from a Moving Cart
demos.desc: A cart fires a ball straight up. At constant speed the ball lands back in the launcher; make the cart speed up or brake and it misses. Watch from the ground or from the cart, with velocity vectors and strobe images.

demos.title: Springs and Oscillations
demos.desc: Pull a mass on a spring and let go: simple harmonic motion, a period that ignores the amplitude, three kinds of damping, a driven oscillator sweeping through resonance, and two coupled masses trading energy in beats.

demos.title: Pendulum
demos.desc: Time a pendulum with a photogate and measure g from how its period depends on length. Then see that mass doesn't matter, large swings take longer, and a swinging rod beats a simple pendulum.

demos.title: Rotational Dynamics
demos.desc: A falling mass spins a turntable. Time the drop, find the angular acceleration, and measure moments of inertia from a plot of torque against angular acceleration.

demos.title: Gyroscope Precession
demos.desc: A spinning wheel held up at one end swings round instead of falling. See the torque turn the angular momentum, and measure how the precession rate depends on the spin.

demos.title: Potential Energy Curves
demos.desc: Read motion off a graph of U(x): drag the energy line and watch the particle speed up, slow down and turn around. Springs, roller coasters, a double well, a molecule, a pendulum, or a curve you draw yourself, with phase space.

demos.title: Sources of Energy
demos.desc: How much uranium, gas, coal, food, battery, falling water or wind it takes to supply a given amount of energy: energy per kilogram across eight powers of ten.

demos.title: Rotation and Torque
demos.desc: Push a door near the hinge and at the handle, race a hoop, disk and sphere down a ramp, spin a skater who pulls her arms in, and balance a seesaw.

demos.title: Hanging Chains and Arches
demos.desc: Drag the ends of a hanging chain and compare its catenary with a parabola, follow the tension along it, then flip it into an arch that stands in pure compression, like the Gateway Arch.

demos.title: Impulse and Momentum
demos.desc: Bounce a cart off a force sensor and show that the area under the force against time graph equals its change of momentum. Soft and stiff bumpers give the same impulse with very different forces.

demos.title: Collisions and Momentum
demos.desc: Crash carts on an air track and pucks on an air table: momentum is always conserved, kinetic energy only when the bounce is elastic. Also an explosion, Newton's cradle, and why a soft bumper lowers the peak force for the same impulse.

demos.title: Center of Mass
demos.desc: Find the centre of mass of masses on a plate, watch a firework's pieces keep its centre of mass on the original parabola, and walk along a boat that slides back.

demos.title: Rocket Propulsion
demos.desc: Burn fuel and watch the rocket get lighter and faster: the rocket equation in deep space, then a launch against gravity, a rocket too heavy to lift off at first, and why a slow burn wastes fuel.

demos.title: Pendulums and Chaos
demos.desc: Big swings take longer than the small angle formula says. Hang a second pendulum from the first for normal modes at low energy and chaos at high energy: 100 copies a millionth of a radian apart fan out, and a Poincaré section shows islands in a chaotic sea.

demos.title: Fluids: Pressure, Buoyancy and Flow
demos.desc: Drag a pressure probe down a tank, drop blocks that float or sink, weigh one in an overflow can like Archimedes, see an iceberg float 89% under, watch a Venturi tube trade pressure for speed, and aim Torricelli's jet.

demos.title: Falling Ball Viscometer
demos.desc: Time balls falling through glycerol, oil or water and measure viscosity with Stokes' law. Then find where it fails: tube walls and fast, high Reynolds number flow.

demos.title: Static Equilibrium
demos.desc: Balance a seesaw, walk a painter off the end of a plank until it tips, hang a sign from a strut and cable, and climb a ladder until it slips, with every force drawn to scale.

demos.title: Stress and Strain
demos.desc: Hang loads on a thin metal wire and read the stretch on a dial gauge. Find Young's modulus from the straight part, then pass the yield point, see the wire stay longer, and load it until it snaps.

demos.title: States of Matter
demos.desc: Heat a crystal of argon atoms under a piston and watch the bonds between them break: the temperature holds still while it melts and again while it boils, because the heat goes into the bonds. A beaker view heats ice to steam with the textbook's specific and latent heats.

demos.title: Blackbody Radiation
demos.desc: Explore thermal emission across temperatures, test Planck’s spectrum, Wien’s displacement law and Stefan–Boltzmann scaling, and connect the results to visible color.

demos.title: Gas in a Box
demos.desc: Watch pressure and temperature emerge from molecules hitting the walls, speeds relax to Maxwell-Boltzmann, and a moving piston heat the gas.

demos.title: Heat Engine Cycles
demos.desc: Run an ideal gas around Carnot, Otto, Diesel, Stirling and Brayton cycles, or drag your own: the PV loop's area is the net work, a T–S diagram shows the heat, and no engine beats the Carnot limit. Reverse it for a refrigerator.

demos.title: Ising Model
demos.desc: Spins on a lattice that each favor their neighbors: cool through T<sub>c</sub> and order appears on its own, with fractal domains at T<sub>c</sub>, hysteresis, and heat capacity and susceptibility measured against Onsager's exact solution.

demos.title: Belousov–Zhabotinsky Reaction
demos.desc: A chemical clock: a stirred beaker oscillates on a limit cycle, an unstirred dish carries target and spiral waves, and a flow reactor goes through period doubling to chaos.

demos.title: Charging by Induction
demos.desc: Charge two metal spheres without touching them: bring a charged rod near, separate the spheres or ground one, then take the rod away. Every mark on the spheres comes from an exact electrostatics solution.

demos.title: Coulomb Sandbox
demos.desc: Drag point charges and watch the field lines, equipotentials and potential update live, as a 2D map or a rotatable 3D landscape.

demos.title: Charges in Magnetic Fields
demos.desc: Launch protons, electrons and alphas into a magnetic field and watch them circle at a period that doesn't depend on speed. Build a velocity selector, a mass spectrometer that separates neon isotopes, and a cyclotron.

demos.title: Faraday's and Lenz's Laws
demos.desc: Push a magnet into a coil and watch the flux, EMF and current, with the coil pushing back. Move it fast or slow and the same total charge flows. Spin a generator coil and slide a bar along rails.

demos.title: Induced Electric Fields
demos.desc: A long solenoid seen end on with a changing current: the electric field it induces circles the axis, inside and in the empty space outside. Drag a closed path and compare the circulation of E with the rate of change of flux.

demos.title: Induction at Work
demos.desc: Three devices that run on Faraday's law: shake a magnet through a coil to charge a flashlight, draw with a magnetic pen on a grid of wires, and swipe a card's magnetic stripe past a reading head.

demos.title: Gauss's Law
demos.desc: Drag charges in and out of a Gaussian surface of any shape and watch the flux: Q<sub>enc</sub>/ε₀ from a real numerical surface integral, zero for charges outside. Then the sphere, line and plane derivations step by step.
tags: field of a sphere, line and plane

demos.title: Magnetic Fields of Currents
demos.desc: Drag wires and watch their fields add and the forces between them, test Ampère's law on any loop with a numerical integral, and bend the current into a loop or a solenoid computed exactly from Biot–Savart.

demos.title: Magnetism in Matter
demos.desc: Fill a long solenoid with aluminum, bismuth, liquid oxygen, water or iron and compare B with the coil's own field: tiny para and diamagnetic changes, the field needed to float water, and iron's hysteresis loop.

demos.title: Electromagnetic Waves
demos.desc: A plane wave in 3D with E, B and the Poynting vector, polarization from linear to circular, the energy and pressure of sunlight and a laser, the full spectrum, and a dipole antenna launching waves with exact field lines.

demos.title: Electrostatics at Work
demos.desc: A Van de Graaff dome charging until the air breaks down, an ink jet printer steering charged drops onto paper, and a smokestack precipitator pulling charged dust out of a gas flow.

demos.title: Capacitors and Dielectrics
demos.desc: Pull the plates apart and slide in a dielectric with the battery connected or not, and follow Q, V, E, C and the energy, including the work your hand does. Field lines come from a real solution with fringing at the edges.

demos.title: Circuits
demos.desc: Everything in one place: build DC circuits with batteries, bulbs and meters, charge a capacitor through a resistor, drive an RLC circuit to resonance, and watch circuits ring down on their own.

demos.title: Magnetism from Relativity
demos.desc: Ride along with a charge beside a current and length contraction turns the magnetic force into an electric one. Then Einstein's magnet and loop, the field of a fast charge, and how E and B transform.

demos.title: Displacement Current
demos.desc: Charge a capacitor and move an Amperian loop along the wire and into the gap. Stretch its surface between the plates and see why Maxwell added ε₀ dΦE/dt to Ampère's law.

demos.title: Resistivity of a Wire
demos.desc: Slide a clip along a wire, read the voltmeter and work out its resistance. Change length, thickness, metal and temperature, then fit your readings to find the resistivity and its temperature coefficient.

demos.title: Household Wiring and Electrical Safety
demos.desc: A 120 V kitchen branch circuit with hot, neutral and ground wires: overload it, short it, or let a worn cord touch a metal case, and see when the breaker or the GFCI trips and what a person feels.

demos.title: Force on a Current
demos.desc: Weigh the force on a current-carrying wire with a magnet on a balance and find B, then see the forces on a loop make a torque, and add a commutator to build a DC motor.

demos.title: Eddy Currents: Magnet in a Pipe
demos.desc: Drop a strong magnet down copper, aluminium and plastic pipes side by side. Currents induced in the metal walls push back by Lenz's law, and the magnet drifts down at a slow terminal speed.

demos.title: Standing Waves
demos.desc: Add two traveling waves into a standing wave, find the harmonics of a guitar string, drive it into resonance, pluck it and see which harmonics vanish, compare open and closed pipes, hear two close tones beat, and float beads at the pressure nodes of a 40 kHz acoustic levitator.

demos.title: Linear Density of a String
demos.desc: Hang masses on a string driven by a vibrator, or sweep the driving frequency with a fixed mass, find the resonances and count the loops, then get the string's mass per metre from the slope of f against n or T against 1/n².

demos.title: Doppler Effect and Shock Waves
demos.desc: Drag a source and an observer through the wavefronts: hear an ambulance's pitch fall as it passes, break the sound barrier into a Mach cone and a sonic boom, then switch to light for redshift, blueshift and the transverse Doppler effect.

demos.title: Timbre and Harmonics
demos.desc: Build a tone from its harmonics and hear it: square, sawtooth and triangle waves, instrument-like spectra, the missing fundamental, and why phase barely matters.

demos.title: Sound Waves and the Speed of Sound
demos.desc: What a sound wave is: watch the air in a tube swing back and forth with the pressure a quarter cycle behind, then time a clap between two microphones to measure the speed of sound, and race sound through 25 gases, liquids and solids over a course up to 10 km long.

demos.title: Kundt's Tube
demos.desc: Stroke a metal rod and the cork dust in a tube of gas gathers at the nodes: one frequency, two wavelengths, and the speed of sound in both the gas and the metal.

demos.title: Sound Intensity and Decibels
demos.desc: Walk a sound level meter away from a loudspeaker in an open field: the level drops 6 dB every time the distance doubles, and two equal sources add only 3 dB.

demos.title: Room Acoustics and the Anechoic Chamber
demos.desc: Clap in a hard room and time the echoes dying away, add absorbing panels and test Sabine's formula, then line the walls with wedges for an anechoic chamber with a clean 1/r² and a low frequency cutoff.

demos.title: Resonators
demos.desc: What sets an instrument's pitch: find the speed of sound with a resonance tube, pluck and bow a string, and blow across a bottle as you fill it, with sound.

demos.title: Acoustic Levitation
demos.desc: Hold beads in midair with two bowls of 40 kHz speakers: traps in the standing wave, the Gor'kov force against gravity, and beads carried along by shifting the phase.

demos.title: Chladni Plates
demos.desc: Drive a metal plate at its resonances and watch sand gather on the nodal lines: square and circular plates, a response curve with every mode, a 3D view and Chladni's law.

demos.title: Energy and Power of a Wave
demos.desc: Send waves along a string into an absorber and read the power meter as you change the amplitude, the frequency and the tension, then find how the power a wave carries depends on each.

demos.title: Two Speaker Interference
demos.desc: Walk a microphone across a room with two speakers playing the same tone, find the loud and quiet lines from the path difference, and get the wavelength and the speed of sound.

demos.title: Ultrasound: Echoes and Blood Flow
demos.desc: Time the echoes of an ultrasound pulse from the boundaries between fat, muscle and bone to find their depths, then point the beam at an artery and get the blood speed from the Doppler shift.

demos.title: Huygens's Principle
demos.desc: Race light through water, glass and diamond to see v = c/n, then build new wavefronts from wavelets to explain reflection, refraction and Snell's law, total internal reflection, and the spreading of a wave through an opening.

demos.title: Optics Bench
demos.desc: Drag lenses, mirrors, prisms and light sources. Rays bend and bounce live, and images form where they cross.

demos.title: The Eye
demos.desc: Watch the eye change its power to keep an image on the retina, find the near and far points of normal, nearsighted, farsighted and older eyes, and prescribe the glasses that correct them.

demos.title: Polarization
demos.desc: Send light through polarizers and wave plates and watch the electric field after each one: Malus's law, the three polarizer surprise, circular light from a quarter wave plate, and glare at Brewster's angle.

demos.title: Thin Film Interference
demos.desc: See why soap bubbles and oil slicks are colored: two reflections from a thin film add or cancel, computed exactly with the reflected color of white light, plus the black film, air wedge fringes, Newton's rings and anti reflection coatings.

demos.title: Diffraction Grating
demos.desc: Shine lasers, an RGB module, white light or H, He, Ne, Hg and Na lamps through gratings from 100 to 1000 lines/mm, a CD or a DVD. See the orders land on the wall, overlapping rainbows and missing orders, then measure a spot with calipers to find the wavelength.
